mutant.description: The load-bearing assertion of O7-AC1 is that the cadence read from the PRODUCER differs from what the artifact's own timestamp would tell you -- the precise trap the face was cut against. The control is a two-instrument split on independent substrates: the DECLARED plane (Terraform text at HEAD, infra/aws/terraform/globgrph/item2a.tf:404-409) and the APPLIED plane (the live EventBridge rule set via aws events list-rules), which share no artifact and no code path.
mutant.expected: If the producer is genuinely unscheduled, the Terraform declaration must say the flag was removed AND the live schedule plane must contain no rule that fires it. If instead a schedule existed and had merely failed, the Terraform would still declare it and the live sweep would return a matching rule in some state (ENABLED or DISABLED), and the two instruments would disagree.
mutant.observed: Both instruments agree and neither inherited the other's claim: Terraform declares the flag REVERTED (deleted) 2026-07-16 with its reason and its ruling id; the live sweep returns 142 rules of which 5 name-match globgrph|heat|snap|trino and 0 fire the code_heat producer, while four sibling producers on the same federation DO carry nightly crons -- so the sweep is capable of finding a producer rule when one exists, which is the positive control on the negative result. Separately, the artifact-mtime instrument was run as the deliberately-wrong arm: it returns 2026-07-16, a number that coincides with the true last run and would therefore have been mistaken for a cadence answer; it cannot distinguish 'ran once and stopped by design' from 'nightly, last 50 days broken', which is exactly why the face forbids it as the basis.
